quotes.text: Settlement timing: Up to 2 business days (T+2)
You can’t cancel a pending Zip refund.
Zip manages disputes for US Zip payments directly.
You have 12 calendar days from dispute creation to respond.

old_evidence.text: Customers have up to 180 calendar days from the date of purchase to file a dispute.
You can’t give return credits in cash unless required by law.

findings: New raw lines 9-28, 112-154 and 231-256 document a single-use domestic AU/US method in AUD or USD, eligible merchants and Connect platforms or marketplaces, B2B/B2C labels and country-specific MCC screening. Dynamic Payment Element and Checkout Session display checks shipping-country code then client IP geocoding. The later product/API blocks show Checkout payment mode (no subscription or setup), Payment Links, Payment Element and in-app support, but no Express Checkout, recurring, manual capture, SetupIntent, future usage or off-session use. May describes manual versus dynamically managed setup and the same account/customer markets, no recurring/manual capture, and common Checkout mode restrictions (old raw lines 11-91).

New raw lines 265-291 describe buyer billing information, a Stripe-hosted redirect to Zip on desktop or mobile, eligibility assessment, account sign-in/creation, payment-plan selection and acceptance, automatic return, and Stripe's reported success/failure. Old raw lines 8-10 describe the same central eligibility/authentication and buyer-repays-Zip flow. Confirmation is immediate in new raw line 13. New raw line 14 documents settlement up to T+2, distinct from authorization, return or actual payout, and old raw lines 33-35 call payout timing standard. Zip creates the statement descriptors for buyer installments; Stripe account or payment descriptors do not control them.

New raw lines 132-145 retain Zip Pay and Zip Money in AU and US Pay in 4 with a fee, first payment at checkout and three fortnightly payments. AU can apply a card to a purchase portion over available credit. Zip Money can reach AUD 50,000 subject to approval and retailer availability, and interest-free periods longer than three months or credit above AUD 5,000 require retailer qualification. The May baseline describes a typical AUD 1,000-5,000 credit range, with potential AUD 50,000, and instructs merchants to contact support for those higher/longer terms (old raw lines 93-111).

New raw lines 172-195 retain full and partial refund ability and 180 calendar days from payment, and specify pending asynchronous refunds, typical 3-5 business days after Zip processes refund confirmation, no pending cancellation, refund.updated/refund.failed, returned Stripe balance on failure and merchant recovery by another method. For US full returns, Zip cancels unpaid installments and restores paid portions to the original method; partial refunds reduce unpaid installments and return any excess. AU refunds credit available Zip balance.

New raw lines 197-229 specify AU's 180-day filing window, merchant-first process after 14 days from purchase, Stripe withholding disputed amount and fee, Stripe notifications and 12 calendar days from dispute creation for merchant evidence. The AU Stripe balance is restored for a merchant win or permanently charged on customer win. Zip manages US disputes, notifications, responses and outcomes directly. The November page reports no fixed AU decision timeframe and gives API evidence routing.

New raw lines 23-110 add actual country MCC tables, including MCC 6513 prohibited in AU and restricted in US with possible additional information. Old raw lines 113-125 link the separate country terms and already require country-specific branding. New raw lines 258-263 retain the branding requirement. Preserve old raw lines 169-185 as dated delivery/recordkeeping/no-surcharge/US location and no gift-card provisions, including the cash-credit legal exception omitted by current summary line 30. Absence of these detailed terms in November is not rescission.
substantive_changes: November adds structured access/timing, account models, domestic boundaries, country-specific MCCs, qualification and explicit product/API capabilities (new raw lines 10-156 and 231-256), country-specific dispute/refund operations (lines 172-229), and descriptor ownership (lines 283-285). T+2 settlement is more specific and differently scoped than the May standard payout label. US dispute routing and explicit AU evidence timing are operationally material.

November changes presentation from the older property list, combined country/limit table, and video/intro navigation to eligibility, payment options, capabilities and a four-step flow. The stable product plans, dynamic filtering, setup/capture exclusions and branding language must retain their own scope. Removed examples and requirements remain dated historical evidence.

A merchant would also lack refund irreversibility, role and timing, method setup restrictions and country MCC information. Preserve the Stripe index lines 350-351 and 747, Stripe BNPL concept lines 112-124 and 272-273, reciprocal summary route, and both raw captures. Keep the separate integration guide linked.

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/zip documents single-use domestic AU and US Zip payments in AUD or USD. New raw lines 9-291 place merchant and Connect eligibility, country-specific MCC screening, Checkout payment mode and dynamic display ahead of the buyer's Zip eligibility and payment-plan authorization. Zip or its flow returns the buyer and Stripe reports success or failure immediately. Settlement is separately described as up to two business days. Old raw lines 8-185 share the customer repayment and markets, but give standard payout wording and one generic dispute flow. November details pending and irreversible refunds and distinct US Zip-managed versus Australian merchant/Stripe disputes. source-stripe-zip.md preserves products and historical limits but generalizes dispute rules, omits refund operations and the new MCC tables, and needs dated eligibility qualifications.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/zip, old raw lines 11-185 and new raw lines 10-291 distinguish reorganized layout and links from new substantive detail. Preserve Australian merchant-first disputes at 14 days from purchase and filing within 180 days, twelve calendar days from creation for evidence, and the US Zip-direct path. Keep the 180-day refund window separate from disputes, including typical asynchronous timing and country-specific credit destination. Preserve the Australian Zip Pay AUD 0.50 prose and AUD 1 table conflict and the provisional-access versus invite-only matrix wording. Keep May delivery, recordkeeping and other dated terms alongside new MCC tables. source-stripe-zip.md should retain both raw captures and reciprocal Stripe index and Stripe BNPL concept links.
